findings.title: toolStore.ts is a zero-importer duplicate of artStore's tool-modifier slice
findings.claim: `useToolStore` is a complete zustand store (mirror / ditherPattern / ditherSecondary / pixelPerfect plus setMirror/setDither/setPixelPerfect) with ZERO importers anywhere in src/, and every field and setter name is duplicated verbatim by the live `useArtStore`.
findings.evidence: src/renderer/state/toolStore.ts:14 defines `useToolStore`. Grep for `useToolStore` across all of src/ returns exactly one hit — the definition line itself (toolStore.ts:14); no component, facet, test or shell module subscribes. Independently confirmed by a module-reachability walk from the three real entries (src/renderer/index.tsx, src/main/index.ts, src/preload/index.ts): toolStore.ts is in the unreached set. Meanwhile src/renderer/state/artStore.ts:29-32 declares `ditherPattern`, `ditherSecondary`, `mirror`, `pixelPerfect` and artStore.ts:56-58 declares `setDither`, `setMirror`, `setPixelPerfect` — identical names, and artStore IS what ArtToolOptions.tsx:183-186 subscribes to. Failure scenario: a future task adds a mirror toggle, autocompletes `useToolStore.setMirror` (the name reads more specific than artStore), and ships a control that flips a store no renderer reads — the toggle moves a number nothing on screen answers to, with no type error and no test failure. This is the exact trap ArtToolOptions.tsx:155-159 documents having already been fallen into once with zoom.
findings.fix: Delete src/renderer/state/toolStore.ts. If the split is wanted later, it must be a slice OF artStore, not a second store.

findings.title: Aether advertises an `editor/ready` event it can never emit — `broadcast` has no callers
findings.claim: The SSE event channel is fully built and wired for subscribers, but `broadcast()` is never called from anywhere, so the `events: ['editor/ready']` capability returned by the `initialize` handshake is a promise the server cannot keep.
findings.evidence: src/main/aether/adapter.ts:94 `export function broadcast(method, params)` — grep for `broadcast` across src/ returns only this definition line; no call site in src/main, src/renderer or src/core. The other two channel functions ARE wired: src/main/mcp-server.ts:14 imports `addSubscriber, removeSubscriber`, calls addSubscriber at mcp-server.ts:110 and removeSubscriber at mcp-server.ts:112. So a client can open the SSE stream and will hold it open forever receiving nothing. adapter.ts:28 `export const EVENTS = ['editor/ready'] as const` is returned to the client at adapter.ts:36 inside `capabilities()`, which adapter.ts:59 returns as the `initialize` result. Failure scenario: an Aether client (per the suite protocol) reads `capabilities.events`, sees `editor/ready`, subscribes to the SSE endpoint and waits for the editor to signal readiness before issuing editor/* calls — it blocks indefinitely, because nothing in Aurora ever writes that frame. `EVENTS` also has no importer outside the same file, so nothing else can emit it either.
findings.fix: Either emit `broadcast('editor/ready')` at the point the renderer finishes opening a project, or remove `EVENTS` from the advertised capabilities and delete `broadcast`. Advertising an event with no emitter is the worse of the two.

findings.title: src/core/art/camera.ts: 8 of its 10 exports are dead; the migration its header promises never happened
findings.claim: Only `screenToWorld` is consumed; `clampZoom`, `worldToScreen`, `pan`, `zoomAtPoint`, `fit`, `zoomToSelection`, `clampPan` and `ZoomBounds` have zero consumers, and the module header's stated purpose (the Map viewport migrating onto this camera) was never carried out.
findings.evidence: The ONLY import of this module anywhere in src/ is src/renderer/components/classic/viewport-math.ts:145 `export { screenToWorld } from '../../../core/art/camera';` — a single-symbol re-export. Grep across src/ for the other names: `clampZoom` 0 hits outside camera.ts, `worldToScreen` 0, `zoomAtPoint` 0, `zoomToSelection` 0, `clampPan` 0 (knip independently flagged clampPan at camera.ts:35). `fit` only matches unrelated locals (BlockTab.tsx:98 `const fit = useBoxSize(fitEl)`, fitCellSize) — never the camera export, which is not imported. The header at camera.ts:1-4 asserts it 'Mirrors the anchored-zoom math viewStore.setZoom already uses, so the Map's navigation is preserved when it migrates onto this' — MapViewport.tsx:706 instead defines its OWN local `function screenToWorld(clientX, clientY)`, and ClassicLevelViewport.tsx:21 pulls the shared one via viewport-math, so the Map never migrated. This is a comment asserting a plan, not a fact.
findings.fix: Move `screenToWorld` (and the `Camera` interface) into components/classic/viewport-math.ts where its one consumer lives, and delete camera.ts. Do not keep the module 'for the migration' — the migration is three direction-changes old.

findings.title: src/core/formats/sprite-mappings.ts is a stale duplicate of the live sprite-mapping parser
findings.claim: This 175-line S2 sprite-mapping parser (`parseSpriteMappings`, `SpriteMappings`, `SpritePiece`) has zero importers; the live parser of the same name is src/core/import/sprite-mappings-import.ts, and every real consumer imports THAT one.
findings.evidence: src/core/formats/sprite-mappings.ts:36 defines `export function parseSpriteMappings`. Its two real callers both import from elsewhere: src/core/import/sprite-import.ts:1 `import { parseSpriteMappings } from './sprite-mappings-import'` (used at sprite-import.ts:97 and :141), and src/core/formats/games/s4.ts:3 `import { parseSpriteMappings } from '../../import/sprite-mappings-import'` (wired as `readMappings` at s4.ts:16). Nothing imports `formats/sprite-mappings` — confirmed by grep over src/ and by the reachability walk, which places it in the unreached set. Failure scenario: two files export a function with the identical name and an overlapping-but-not-identical format contract; a fix applied to the wrong one (the shorter, more obviously-named path) is silently a no-op, and the reviewer sees a correct-looking diff. That is a live foot-gun on the sprite path, not just size.
findings.fix: Delete src/core/formats/sprite-mappings.ts. There must be exactly one `parseSpriteMappings`.

findings.title: Seven exported symbols in otherwise-live files have zero callers
findings.claim: These exports are dead while their host modules are live, so file-level tools and the reachability walk both miss them: buildChunkSurfaceById, decodeObjectArt, TileDeduplicator, ToolButtonGrid, resetClassicObjectArt, IconUndo, IconRedo.
findings.evidence: Each verified by a whole-src grep returning exactly one hit — the definition line — with no internal self-use either: src/core/art/classic-surface-buffer.ts:153 `buildChunkSurfaceById`; src/core/level-classic/object-sprite.ts:33 `decodeObjectArt` (the other 13 exports of that module are live, e.g. renderObjectFrame at :62); src/core/import/tile-dedup.ts:26 `class TileDeduplicator` (the file's other export, `flipTile` at tile-dedup.ts:6, has 3 live importers: core/export/tile-dedup.ts:3, core/agent/budget.ts:3, core/art/composer-buffer.ts:4 — so the FILE must stay, only the class goes); src/renderer/components/art-shared/ToolColumnParts.tsx:41 `ToolButtonGrid` (the file is live — imported by shell/ArtToolOptions.tsx:8, shell/SpriteToolOptions.tsx:7, components/canvas/CanvasMode.tsx:14 — but this one export is unused, including internally); src/renderer/state/classicObjectArtStore.ts:315 `resetClassicObjectArt`; src/renderer/components/ui/icons.tsx:34 `IconUndo` and :35 `IconRedo`. The IconUndo/IconRedo pair is the interesting one: undo/redo icons with no mount is the fingerprint of the deleted Toolbar (removed in 0c42129 'the legacy Toolbar is deleted') — the icons outlived their only consumer. `resetClassicObjectArt` is likewise a test/teardown-shaped helper that no test calls, so the classic object-art cache has no exercised reset path.
findings.fix: Delete the seven symbols (not their host files, except as covered elsewhere). Before deleting resetClassicObjectArt, check whether classicObjectArtStore actually needs a reset on project close — if it does, this is a missing call, not dead code.

findings.title: The design system's entire typography scale is generated but never consumed
findings.claim: 25 of the 55 CSS custom properties emitted by scripts/gen-theme.mjs are never referenced by any `var()` in src/renderer, including all 12 type-scale tokens and all 3 weight tokens — while 227 inline `fontSize` sites hardcode 13 distinct pixel values.
findings.evidence: Set-diff of every `var(--x)` occurrence in src/renderer against every `--x:` definition in src/renderer/styles/theme.css yields these unreferenced tokens: --text-{xs,sm,base,md,lg,xl,2xl}-{size,line} (14), --weight-{regular,medium,semibold} (3), --space-0, --space-9, and --accent-{aurora,aether,crucible,empyrean,oracle,seraph} (6). They are not consumed indirectly either: src/renderer/components/ui/theme.ts:4-16 is the ONLY typed bridge to these variables and its `T` map exposes surfaces, the text ramp, one accent, fonts, --space-1..8 and the radii — it deliberately omits every type-scale, weight and sibling-accent token. Against that, src/renderer carries 227 `fontSize` occurrences with hardcoded values (73x 11, 58x 10, 50x 12, 18x 13, 12x 9, 4x 8, 3x 16, 3x 14, 2x 18, and one each of 7/15/20/36) and 50 hardcoded `fontWeight` values (40x 600, 5x 700, 4x 500). The generator itself is NOT dead — I ran `node scripts/gen-theme.mjs` and it regenerated theme.css byte-identically (git status stayed clean), resolving tokens via the megaforge->empyrean symlink. So the pipeline works; the tokens simply have no consumer. Fifteen of the 25 (the scale + weights) are Aurora's own type system going unused; the six sibling-tool accents are a legitimate contract dump and should not be counted as debt.
findings.fix: Either extend `T` in components/ui/theme.ts with the scale (fsXs..fs2xl, wRegular/wMedium/wSemibold) and migrate the 227 sites, or drop the scale from gen-theme.mjs's output. Shipping a type scale that 227 call sites ignore is the more expensive of the two states.

findings.title: core/model/types.ts is a compat barrel whose value re-exports are all dead
findings.claim: The barrel re-exports 16 runtime symbols and 15 types from s4-types, but its five importers consume only Tile, Color, Palette, PaletteLine and TileRef — every value re-export (createSection, createSectionTileGrid, createChunkDef, packNametableWord, unpackNametableWord, SECTION_TILES_*, BLOCK_*, BLOCKS_PER_SECTION, SF_*) reaches nobody through this path.
findings.evidence: src/core/model/types.ts:19-35 re-exports the value block; :2-18 re-exports the type block. All five importers of 'model/types' take only the primitives: src/renderer/canvas/TileRenderer.ts:1 (Tile, PaletteLine, Color), src/core/formats/palette.ts:1 (Color, Palette, PaletteLine), src/core/import/color-quantize.ts:1 (Palette, Color — itself dead per A6), src/core/formats/tiles.ts:1 (Tile), src/core/import/tile-dedup.ts:1 (Tile, TileRef). The live consumers of the re-exported values go straight to the source instead: src/renderer/agent/agent-handler.ts:7 imports `packNametableWord, unpackNametableWord, createChunkDef` from s4-types, and createChunkDef is defined at s4-types.ts:156. The legacy `Block`/`BlockRef`/`Chunk` interfaces declared locally at types.ts:46/50/58 are imported by nobody. Low severity, but it is a second name for the model surface, and A4/A6 show what two names for one thing cost here.
findings.fix: Reduce types.ts to the five primitives its importers actually use plus TileRef, drop the value re-export block and the unused legacy interfaces — or repoint the five importers at s4-types and delete the barrel.
